newsitem.title: USA: Electric Lightwave sues U.S. West.
newsitem.headline: Electric Lightwave sues U.S. West.

text.p: Electric Lightwave Inc, a provider of telecommunications, Monday said it filed an antitrust suit against U.S. West Communications Inc, alleging it is illegally blocking competition for local service.
In a statement, Electric Lightwave claims U.S. West has failed to provide adequate interconnection services facilities for it to offer quality services to its customers.
Electric Lightwave, based in Vancouver, Wash., is a subsidiary of Citizens Utilities Co, and U.S. West Communications Inc is a unit of U S West Communications Group, a component of U S West Inc.

Electric Lightwave said U.S. West's actions led to call blockage, busy signals, disconnects and other problems for its customers. It is seeking an unspecified amount of damages which it said "could run into the millions of dollars." It is the first antitrust suit filed against one of the so-called Baby Bells, under the federal Telecommunications Act of 1996 requiring cooperation for local phone service.

David Beigie, chief spokesman for U S West, said the company has not seen the lawsuit. He noted U S West has 245 agreements or pending agreements with competitors for local service throughout its 14-state region.
"We feel like we are doing quite a bit to open up local competition," he said.

In addition to damages, Electric Lightwave is seeking an injunction to prevent U S West from using its facilities or software or arranging its system in a way that puts lower priority on calls of Electric Lightwave customers.
